- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Reduce sigmoid MoE inference routing overhead for Nemotron Nano, Super, and Ultra while preserving bit-exact expert indices and FP32 probabilities relative to the original compiled router.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Implementation

- For small top-k, including Nano's 128 experts / top-6 configuration, fuse sigmoid, expert selection, normalization, and scaling into one kernel
- For larger top-k, including Super/Ultra's 512 experts / top-22 configuration, use parallel expert selection while retaining the original compiled sigmoid and probability computation
- Tune launch configurations for small decode batches and larger prefill batches
- Preserve existing fallback behavior for unsupported configurations and environments

For larger top-k, a scoped runtime dispatch mode replaces only aten.topk. The original compiled graph, cache lookup, and normalization kernels remain unchanged. This preserves the reference reduction order, including when reusing an existing compiler cache

The optimization requires Triton tl.topk and PyTorch's private TorchDispatchMode.ignore_compile_internals hook for the large-top-k path. When these capabilities are unavailable, routing retains the original compiled implementation.

## Performance

End-to-end batch generation speedup against main `db3a6cd8a` (candidate `3014eea22`):

| Model | BS16 speedup | BS32 speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| Nemotron Nano | 1.053x | 1.030x |
| Nemotron Super | 1.031x | 1.016x |
| Nemotron Ultra | 1.015x | 1.012x |

Measurement setup:

- Two nodes, 8 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs, TP8 / EP8 / ETP1; official BF16 checkpoints converted to Megatron Core, FP32 router, FA4, decode CUDA Graphs, NVLS dispatcher; batch-invariant mode and prefix caching disabled
- 16 or 32 requests with 32–33 prompt tokens and exactly 128 greedy output tokens each
- Three independent allocations per model. Each runs four fresh processes per batch size (baseline → candidate → candidate → baseline at BS16, reversed at BS32) with five timed generations per process
- Speedup = baseline / candidate latency, using the mean of the two per-process medians; the table shows the geometric mean of the three allocation ratios and a 95% t interval on the log ratios. All samples are retained
- Triton autotune selection is pinned for both versions (`--triton-autotune-mode pinned`), so fresh processes generate comparable tokens. Generated tokens were identical between baseline and candidate in every allocation
- Timing starts after request enqueue and ends when all requests finish (prefill and decode). Model loading, warmup and tokenization are excluded

## Validation

All tested routing comparisons require identical expert indices and identical FP32 probability bits. No numerical tolerances were relaxed

- 87 targeted tests passed on each of 8 ranks
- 120 TP8 router cases passed, covering Nano, Super, and Ultra dimensions with 2, 32, 256, 512, and 8192 tokens per rank
- 292 production-path comparisons passed with both reused and fresh compiler caches, including 36 CUDA Graph replay checks with updated inputs
- 3,552 candidate router comparisons using real checkpoint weights and activations passed bit-exact comparison
- Generated tokens matched across all ranks, runs, and versions for all three models

Tests also cover tied scores, strided expert bias, fallback configurations, gradient-enabled execution, and preservation of the batch-invariant path.

Bit-exact replay tests were added or updated, and the kernel module is registered in the determinism manifest.

After rebasing onto main `db3a6cd8a`, the router, determinism replay and manifest tests (362 per rank) pass on each of 4 GB300 ranks, and the end-to-end runs below generated the same tokens as main in every allocation.

Validation used PyTorch 2.12.1+cu130 and Triton 3.7.1 on GB300. Checkpoint comparisons validate the original and optimized Megatron Core paths; full Hugging Face-versus-Megatron forward parity was not tested.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,301 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Sigmoid top-k routing kernels for inference.
+
+Replaces the compiled ``topk_routing_with_score_function`` sequence for sigmoid
+scores with an expert bias (an inductor sigmoid+bias kernel, aten ``topk``, and
+two inductor gather/normalize kernels) with one launch for top-k below eight.
+Expert selection and ordering match ``torch.topk(..., sorted=False)``, and
+probabilities match the compiled left-fold normalization bitwise. Larger top-k
+uses parallel expert selection while preserving the compiled sigmoid and
+normalization graph. Batch-invariant routing does not use these kernels.
+"""
+
+from typing import Optional
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import torch
+from torch.utils._python_dispatch import TorchDispatchMode
+
+from megatron.core.utils import null_decorator
+
+try:
+    import triton
+    import triton.language as tl
+
+    HAVE_TRITON = True
+except ImportError:
+    HAVE_TRITON = False
+
+if not HAVE_TRITON:
+    triton = MagicMock()
+    triton.jit = null_decorator
+    tl = MagicMock()
+
+
+def is_sigmoid_topk_supported(num_experts: int, topk: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether the fused path preserves the compiled router's normalization order."""
+    return 1 < topk < 8 and topk <= num_experts <= 512
+
+
+def is_topk_scores_supported(num_experts: int, topk: int) -> bool:
+    """Whether parallel top-k selection is available for this inference shape."""
+    return (
+        HAVE_TRITON
+        and hasattr(tl, "topk")
+        and hasattr(TorchDispatchMode, "ignore_compile_internals")
+        and 8 <= topk <= min(32, num_experts)
+        and num_experts <= 512
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _topk_scores_kernel(
+    scores_ptr,
+    values_ptr,
+    indices_ptr,
+    NUM_EXPERTS: tl.constexpr,
+    EXPERTS_POW2: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPK: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPK_POW2: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Parallel cutoff selection with aten's unsorted expert order."""
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, EXPERTS_POW2)
+    valid = cols < NUM_EXPERTS
+    scores = tl.load(scores_ptr + row.to(tl.int64) * NUM_EXPERTS + cols, valid, other=0.0)
+    bits = scores.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+    keys = tl.where(bits >= 0, bits, bits ^ 0x7FFFFFFF)
+    keys = tl.where(valid, keys, -2147483648)
+    largest = tl.topk(keys, TOPK_POW2, dim=0)
+    kth = tl.sum(tl.where(tl.arange(0, TOPK_POW2) == TOPK - 1, largest, 0))
+
+    # Use only the cutoff from topk. Emit above-cutoff columns first, followed
+    # by enough cutoff ties to reach k; both groups follow input column order.
+    above = (keys > kth) & valid
+    tied = (keys == kth) & valid
+    num_above = tl.sum(above.to(tl.int32), axis=0)
+    tied_rank = tl.cumsum(tied.to(tl.int32), axis=0)
+    selected_tied = tied & (tied_rank <= TOPK - num_above)
+    slot = tl.where(above, tl.cumsum(above.to(tl.int32), axis=0) - 1, num_above + tied_rank - 1)
+    offsets = row.to(tl.int64) * TOPK + slot
+    tl.store(indices_ptr + offsets, cols.to(tl.int64), above | selected_tied)
+    tl.store(values_ptr + offsets, scores, above | selected_tied)
+
+
+def topk_scores(scores: torch.Tensor, topk: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Unsorted top-k for contiguous finite fp32 inference scores on CUDA.
+
+    Called at execution time by ``ParallelTopKMode`` so the original compiled
+    router, including its cached normalization kernels, stays unchanged.
+    """
+    assert scores.is_cuda and scores.ndim == 2 and scores.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert scores.is_contiguous()
+    num_tokens, num_experts = scores.shape
+    assert is_topk_scores_supported(num_experts, topk)
+    values = scores.new_empty((num_tokens, topk))
+    indices = scores.new_empty((num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.int64)
+    if num_tokens:
+        _topk_scores_kernel[(num_tokens,)](
+            scores,
+            values,
+            indices,
+            NUM_EXPERTS=num_experts,
+            EXPERTS_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(num_experts),
+            TOPK=topk,
+            TOPK_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(topk),
+            # Wide prefill batches expose enough row-level parallelism to use
+            # fewer warps per CTA. Tiny decode batches benefit from four warps.
+            num_warps=1 if num_experts == 512 and num_tokens >= 1024 else 4,
+        )
+    return values, indices
+
+
+class ParallelTopKMode(TorchDispatchMode):
+    """Replace aten top-k only while executing the original compiled router.
+
+    Replacing top-k in the FX graph changes its cache key. A new graph can
+    autotune normalization differently from a cached reference, changing
+    probability bits even if its mathematical expressions are unchanged.
+    This mode leaves tracing, compilation and cache lookup untouched; only
+    the runtime top-k call is replaced. The selected values and indices are
+    identical, so the same compiled probability kernels see the same inputs.
+    """
+
+    @classmethod
+    def ignore_compile_internals(cls):
+        """Keep this mode out of Dynamo tracing and cache keys; intercept only at runtime."""
+        return True
+
+    def __torch_dispatch__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        kwargs = kwargs or {}
+        if func is torch.ops.aten.topk.default:
+            scores, topk, *options = args
+            dim = options[0] if options else kwargs.get("dim", -1)
+            largest = options[1] if len(options) > 1 else kwargs.get("largest", True)
+            sorted_output = options[2] if len(options) > 2 else kwargs.get("sorted", True)
+            if (
+                scores.is_cuda
+                and scores.ndim == 2
+                and scores.dtype == torch.float32
+                and scores.is_contiguous()
+                and dim in (1, -1)
+                and largest
+                and not sorted_output
+                and is_topk_scores_supported(scores.shape[1], topk)
+            ):
+                return topk_scores(scores, topk)
+        return func(*args, **kwargs)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _sigmoid_topk_kernel(
+    logits_ptr,
+    expert_bias_ptr,
+    probs_ptr,
+    indices_ptr,
+    num_tokens,
+    scaling_factor,
+    NUM_EXPERTS: tl.constexpr,
+    BIAS_STRIDE: tl.constexpr,
+    EXPERTS_POW2: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPK: tl.constexpr,
+    APPLY_SCALING: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_T: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Top-k of sigmoid(logits) + bias, probabilities from sigmoid(logits).
+
+    Matches the compiled reference bit for bit:
+      * selection and order follow aten topk(sorted=False): a row's k-th largest
+        key under radix (total float) order, then every column above it in
+        ascending column order, then columns equal to it in ascending order;
+      * probabilities are (s_j / (s_0 + ... + s_{k-1} + 1e-20)) * scaling_factor
+        with the sum folded left in output order, as inductor generates it.
+    """
+    rows = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK_T + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_T)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, EXPERTS_POW2)
+    row_mask = rows < num_tokens
+    col_mask = cols < NUM_EXPERTS
+    mask = row_mask[:, None] & col_mask[None, :]
+    rows64 = rows.to(tl.int64)
+
+    logits = tl.load(logits_ptr + rows64[:, None] * NUM_EXPERTS + cols[None, :], mask=mask)
+    bias = tl.load(expert_bias_ptr + cols * BIAS_STRIDE, mask=col_mask)
+    scores = tl.sigmoid(logits)
+    routing_scores = scores + bias[None, :]
+
+    # Radix-order keys: a signed-int compare of these equals aten's unsigned
+    # compare of its converted floats (-0.0 < +0.0). Padding columns get the
+    # smallest key so they are never selected.
+    bits = routing_scores.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+    keys = tl.where(bits >= 0, bits, bits ^ 0x7FFFFFFF)
+    lowest = tl.full([BLOCK_T, EXPERTS_POW2], -2147483648, tl.int32)
+    keys = tl.where(col_mask[None, :], keys, lowest)
+
+    # k-th largest key, counting repeated keys with multiplicity.
+    remaining = keys
+    kth = tl.full([BLOCK_T], -2147483648, tl.int32)
+    found = tl.zeros([BLOCK_T], dtype=tl.int32)
+    for _ in tl.static_range(TOPK):
+        top = tl.max(remaining, axis=1)
+        is_top = remaining == top[:, None]
+        count = tl.sum(is_top.to(tl.int32), axis=1)
+        kth = tl.where((found < TOPK) & (found + count >= TOPK), top, kth)
+        found += count
+        remaining = tl.where(is_top, lowest, remaining)
+
+    above = (keys > kth[:, None]) & col_mask[None, :]
+    tied = (keys == kth[:, None]) & col_mask[None, :]
+    num_above = tl.sum(above.to(tl.int32), axis=1)
+    tied_rank = tl.cumsum(tied.to(tl.int32), axis=1)
+    selected_tied = tied & (tied_rank <= TOPK - num_above[:, None])
+    slot = tl.where(
+        above, tl.cumsum(above.to(tl.int32), axis=1) - 1, num_above[:, None] + tied_rank - 1
+    )
+    selected = above | selected_tied
+
+    out_base = rows64 * TOPK
+    tl.store(
+        indices_ptr + out_base[:, None] + slot,
+        tl.broadcast_to(cols[None, :], (BLOCK_T, EXPERTS_POW2)).to(tl.int64),
+        mask=selected & row_mask[:, None],
+    )
+
+    # Selected sigmoid scores in output order; exactly one column per slot, so
+    # the masked sums are exact. Sigmoid scores are >= +0.0, so folding from
+    # 0.0 reproduces the reference's left fold s_0 + s_1 + ... exactly.
+    total = tl.zeros([BLOCK_T], dtype=tl.float32)
+    for j in tl.static_range(TOPK):
+        total = total + tl.sum(tl.where(selected & (slot == j), scores, 0.0), axis=1)
+    denom = total + 1e-20
+    for j in tl.static_range(TOPK):
+        s_j = tl.sum(tl.where(selected & (slot == j), scores, 0.0), axis=1)
+        p_j = s_j / denom
+        if APPLY_SCALING:
+            p_j = p_j * scaling_factor
+        tl.store(probs_ptr + out_base + j, p_j, mask=row_mask)
+
+
+def sigmoid_topk_routing(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    expert_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    topk: int,
+    scaling_factor: Optional[float] = None,
+    block_tokens: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Dense sigmoid top-k routing with an expert bias.
+
+    Equivalent to ``topk_routing_with_score_function(logits, topk,
+    score_function="sigmoid", expert_bias=expert_bias, scaling_factor=...,
+    dense_output=True)`` evaluated by torch.compile with gradients disabled
+    (which selects with ``torch.topk(sorted=False)``) for finite fp32 logits and bias in
+    the shape range covered by ``is_sigmoid_topk_supported``. Both indices and
+    probabilities match bitwise. Top-k of eight or more is unsupported: its compiled
+    reduction order can depend on autotuning and prior batch shapes. The inference
+    router replaces only top-k selection for those calls, retaining compiled
+    sigmoid and normalization. This kernel is not used in batch-invariant mode.
+
+    Args:
+        logits: [num_tokens, num_experts] fp32 router logits.
+        expert_bias: [num_experts] fp32 routing bias on the same device as logits
+            (selection only). Strided views are supported.
+        topk: experts per token, in [2, 7] and no greater than num_experts.
+        scaling_factor: optional multiplier applied to the normalized probabilities.
+        block_tokens: optional rows per CTA; defaults to one for up to 128 experts
+            and four for wider rows.
+
+    Returns:
+        probs [num_tokens, topk] fp32 and top_indices [num_tokens, topk] int64.
+    """
+    assert logits.dim() == 2 and logits.dtype == torch.float32 and logits.is_contiguous()
+    assert expert_bias.dim() == 1, "expert_bias must be one-dimensional"
+    assert expert_bias.dtype == torch.float32 and expert_bias.numel() == logits.shape[1]
+    assert expert_bias.device == logits.device, "expert_bias and logits must be on the same device"
+    num_tokens, num_experts = logits.shape
+    assert is_sigmoid_topk_supported(num_experts, topk)
+    num_warps = 4
+    if block_tokens is None:
+        # One warp per short row avoids idle rows on decode batches and exposes
+        # more independent CTAs on prefill. Wider rows retain the existing layout.
+        block_tokens = 1 if num_experts <= 128 else 4
+        num_warps = 1 if num_experts <= 128 else 4
+    assert block_tokens > 0 and block_tokens & (block_tokens - 1) == 0
+    probs = torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.float32, device=logits.device)
+    indices = torch.empty(num_tokens, topk, dtype=torch.int64, device=logits.device)
+    if num_tokens == 0:
+        return probs, indices
+    _sigmoid_topk_kernel[(triton.cdiv(num_tokens, block_tokens),)](
+        logits,
+        expert_bias,
+        probs,
+        indices,
+        num_tokens,
+        float(scaling_factor) if scaling_factor else 1.0,
+        NUM_EXPERTS=num_experts,
+        BIAS_STRIDE=expert_bias.stride(0),
+        EXPERTS_POW2=triton.next_power_of_2(num_experts),
+        TOPK=topk,
+        APPLY_SCALING=bool(scaling_factor),
+        BLOCK_T=block_tokens,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+    )
+    return probs, indices

@@ -8,6 +8,13 @@
 
 import torch
 
+from megatron.core.inference.moe.sigmoid_topk import HAVE_TRITON as HAVE_SIGMOID_TOPK_KERNEL
+from megatron.core.inference.moe.sigmoid_topk import (
+    ParallelTopKMode,
+    is_sigmoid_topk_supported,
+    is_topk_scores_supported,
+    sigmoid_topk_routing,
+)
 from megatron.core.inference.utils import InferenceMode
 from megatron.core.jit import jit_fuser
 from megatron.core.packed_seq_params import PackedSeqParams, resolve_cp_group
@@ -1386,6 +1393,46 @@ def _compiled_topk_routing(
             precomputed_indices=precomputed_indices,
         )
 
+    def _uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(
+        self, logits: torch.Tensor, precomputed_indices: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Whether the sigmoid top-k kernels support this inference call.
+
+        It covers sigmoid scores with an expert bias, fp32 logits and supported shapes,
+        with gradients disabled, without group-limited routing, router replay,
+        precomputed indices or TE's fused router; batch-invariant mode keeps its
+        uncompiled reference path. Top-k below eight uses a fully fused kernel
+        matching the compiled left fold. Larger top-k replaces only expert
+        selection, keeping the original compiled probability computation and
+        its autotuned reduction order.
+        """
+        return (
+            HAVE_SIGMOID_TOPK_KERNEL
+            and logits.is_cuda
+            and logits.dtype == torch.float32
+            # InferenceMode is independent of autograd. With gradients enabled,
+            # the reference uses sorted top-k and retains probability gradients.
+            and not torch.is_grad_enabled()
+            and self.score_function == "sigmoid"
+            and self.expert_bias is not None
+            and (
+                is_sigmoid_topk_supported(logits.shape[-1], self.topk)
+                or (
+                    logits.is_contiguous() and is_topk_scores_supported(logits.shape[-1], self.topk)
+                )
+            )
+            and precomputed_indices is None
+            and self.config.moe_router_group_topk is None
+            and not self.config.moe_router_fusion
+            and self.router_replay is None
+            and not is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
+        )
+
+    def _parallel_topk_routing(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        # Reuse the exact compiled callable/cache; intercept only its runtime top-k.
+        with ParallelTopKMode():
+            return self._compiled_topk_routing(*args, **kwargs)
+
     def _forward(
         self,
         input: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1415,6 +1462,15 @@ def _forward(
             if is_batch_invariant_mode_enabled()
             else self._compiled_topk_routing
         )
+        if self._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(logits, precomputed_indices):
+            if is_sigmoid_topk_supported(logits.shape[-1], self.topk):
+                return sigmoid_topk_routing(
+                    logits.contiguous(),
+                    self.expert_bias.float(),
+                    self.topk,
+                    self.config.moe_router_topk_scaling_factor,
+                )
+            routing = self._parallel_topk_routing
         probs, top_indices = routing(
             logits,
             self.topk,

@@ -587,6 +587,43 @@ def fn(routing_map):
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_experts,topk,scaling_factor", [(128, 6, 2.5), (512, 6, 5.0)], ids=["nano", "512-experts"]
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [2, 2048])
+def test_sigmoid_topk_routing_replay(num_experts, topk, scaling_factor, num_tokens):
+    from megatron.core.inference.moe.sigmoid_topk import sigmoid_topk_routing
+
+    seeded()
+    logits = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_experts, device="cuda")
+    expert_bias = torch.randn(num_experts, device="cuda") * 0.05
+    assert_replays_bit_exact(
+        lambda lg, b: sigmoid_topk_routing(lg, b, topk, scaling_factor),
+        (logits, expert_bias),
+        replays=4,
+        backward=False,
+        what=f"sigmoid_topk_routing[tokens={num_tokens}, experts={num_experts}, topk={topk}]",
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", [8, 22, 32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [2, 2048])
+def test_topk_scores_replay(topk, num_tokens):
+    from megatron.core.inference.moe.sigmoid_topk import is_topk_scores_supported, topk_scores
+
+    if not is_topk_scores_supported(512, topk):
+        pytest.skip("Requires Triton topk and runtime dispatch modes")
+    seeded()
+    scores = torch.randn(num_tokens, 512, device="cuda")
+    assert_replays_bit_exact(
+        lambda s: topk_scores(s, topk),
+        (scores,),
+        replays=4,
+        backward=False,
+        what=f"topk_scores[tokens={num_tokens}, topk={topk}]",
+    )
+

+"""Unit tests for megatron.core.inference.moe.sigmoid_topk.
+
+Expert indices and probabilities must match the compiled inference router bit
+for bit. Top-k below eight uses the fused kernel; larger top-k uses parallel
+selection and preserves compiled probabilities. Batch-invariant and autograd
+paths retain their existing behavior.
+"""

+import pytest

+from megatron.core.inference.moe import sigmoid_topk as sigmoid_topk_module
+from megatron.core.inference.moe.sigmoid_topk import (
+    is_topk_scores_supported,
+    sigmoid_topk_routing,
+    topk_scores,

+    pytest.param(128, 6, 2.5, id="nano"),
+    pytest.param(512, 22, 5.0, id="super-ultra"),
+]

+def _assert_matches_compiled(probs, indices, ref_probs, ref_indices, case=None):
+    assert indices.dtype == ref_indices.dtype, case
+    assert probs.dtype == ref_probs.dtype, case
+    assert torch.equal(indices, ref_indices), case
+    assert torch.equal(probs.view(torch.int32), ref_probs.view(torch.int32)), case
+
+
+def _unexpected_fused_routing(*args, **kwargs):
+    pytest.fail("Large top-k must preserve the compiled probability computation")
+
+
+def _compiled_reference(logits, expert_bias, topk, scaling_factor):
+    return InferenceTopKRouter._compiled_topk_routing(
+        logits,
+        topk,
+        False,
+        None,
+        None,
+        scaling_factor,
+        "sigmoid",
+        expert_bias,
+        False,
+        None,
+        True,
+        None,
+    )
+
+
+def _inputs(kind, num_tokens, num_experts, seed):
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    logits = torch.randn(num_tokens, num_experts, generator=gen, device="cuda")
+    bias = torch.randn(num_experts, generator=gen, device="cuda") * 0.05
+    if kind == "wide":
+        logits, bias = logits * 8, bias * 10
+    elif kind == "ties":
+        # Few distinct scores: many rows tie at the k-th value.
+        logits = torch.round(logits * 2) / 2
+        bias = torch.round(bias * 64) / 64
+    elif kind == "all_equal":
+        logits = torch.zeros_like(logits)
+        bias = torch.zeros_like(bias)
+    elif kind == "zero_scores":
+        # sigmoid underflows to +0.0 everywhere but every 7th expert; signed-zero bias.
+        logits = torch.full_like(logits, -200.0)
+        logits[:, ::7] = torch.randn(
+            num_tokens, logits[:, ::7].shape[1], generator=gen, device="cuda"
+        )
+        bias = torch.zeros_like(bias)
+        bias[::2] = -0.0
+    return logits.contiguous(), bias
+
+
+def _strided_expert_bias(bias):
+    # Unused entries must differ from the logical bias to expose contiguous loads.
+    storage = torch.full((2 * bias.numel() + 1,), 10.0, device=bias.device, dtype=bias.dtype)
+    view = storage[1::2]
+    view.copy_(bias)
+    assert view.storage_offset() == 1 and view.stride() == (2,)
+    return view
+

+class TestSigmoidTopkRouting:

+    # One static (experts, top-k, scale) configuration per test, as in a server whose
+    # router configuration is fixed: dynamo specializes top-k, which determines the
+    # compiled probability reduction. Compiling several top-k values without resetting
+    # dynamo can make top-k symbolic and change the reduction order.

+                for num_tokens in (1, 2, 3, 8, 33, 256, 2048):

+    def test_expert_bias_views_match_contiguous(self, num_experts, topk, scaling_factor, layout):

+                # incorrect contiguous load gives every other expert a +10 bias.

+                ref_probs, ref_indices = _compiled_reference(logits, bias, topk, scaling_factor)

+            assert torch.equal(probs.view(torch.int32), contiguous_probs.view(torch.int32))

+        _assert_matches_compiled(probs, indices, ref_probs, ref_indices)
+
+    def test_large_topk_noncontiguous_logits_preserve_compiled_path(self, monkeypatch):
+        router = self._router(
+            num_moe_experts=512, moe_router_topk=22, moe_router_topk_scaling_factor=5.0
+        )
+        logits = torch.randn(512, 4, device="cuda").t()
+        assert not logits.is_contiguous()
+        monkeypatch.setattr(router, "gating", lambda hidden: hidden)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(sigmoid_topk_module, "topk_scores", _unexpected_fused_routing)
+        with InferenceMode.active(), torch.inference_mode():
+            assert not router._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(logits, None)
+            probs, indices = router(logits.unsqueeze(1))
+            ref_probs, ref_indices = _compiled_reference(logits, router.expert_bias, 22, 5.0)
+        _assert_matches_compiled(probs, indices, ref_probs, ref_indices)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_experts,topk,scaling_factor", MODEL_ROUTING_CONFIGS)
+    def test_grad_enabled_preserves_compiled_routing_and_autograd(
+        self, num_experts, topk, scaling_factor
+    ):
+        """InferenceMode alone does not disable gradients or sorted top-k selection."""
+        router = self._router(
+            num_moe_experts=num_experts,
+            moe_router_topk=topk,
+            moe_router_topk_scaling_factor=scaling_factor,
+        )
+        hidden = torch.randn(40, 1, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+        with InferenceMode.active(), torch.enable_grad():
+            probs, indices = router(hidden)
+            ref_probs, ref_indices = _compiled_reference(
+                router.gating(hidden).squeeze(1), router.expert_bias, topk, scaling_factor
+            )
+            assert probs.requires_grad
+            assert torch.equal(indices, ref_indices)
+            assert torch.equal(probs, ref_probs)
+            weights = torch.arange(topk, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+            grad = torch.autograd.grad((probs * weights).sum(), hidden)[0]
+            ref_grad = torch.autograd.grad((ref_probs * weights).sum(), hidden)[0]
+        assert torch.equal(grad, ref_grad)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_experts,topk,scaling_factor", MODEL_ROUTING_CONFIGS)
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 2, 3, 4, 17, 65, 1024, 8192])
+    def test_graph_replay_uses_updated_logits_and_bias(
+        self, monkeypatch, num_experts, topk, scaling_factor, num_tokens
+    ):
+        """Captured routing must read new inputs on every replay, including tied scores."""
+        logits, bias = _inputs("normal", num_tokens, num_experts, seed=17)
+        router = self._router(
+            num_moe_experts=num_experts,
+            moe_router_topk=topk,
+            moe_router_topk_scaling_factor=scaling_factor,
+        )
+        monkeypatch.setattr(router, "gating", lambda logits: logits)
+        if topk >= 8:
+            monkeypatch.setattr(router_module, "sigmoid_topk_routing", _unexpected_fused_routing)
+        router.expert_bias = bias
+        routing_input = logits.unsqueeze(1)
+        with InferenceMode.active(), torch.inference_mode():
+            assert router._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(logits, None) == (
+                topk < 8 or is_topk_scores_supported(num_experts, topk)
+            )
+            # Compile both paths before capture with a fixed top-k specialization.
+            _compiled_reference(logits, bias, topk, scaling_factor)
+            stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+            stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+            with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+                router(routing_input)
+            torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+                probs, indices = router(routing_input)
+            for seed, kind in enumerate(("wide", "ties", "all_equal", "zero_scores", "normal")):
+                new_logits, new_bias = _inputs(kind, num_tokens, num_experts, seed=seed)
+                logits.copy_(new_logits)
+                bias.copy_(new_bias)
+                graph.replay()
+                ref_probs, ref_indices = _compiled_reference(logits, bias, topk, scaling_factor)
+                _assert_matches_compiled(probs, indices, ref_probs, ref_indices, case=kind)
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("num_experts,topk,scaling_factor", MODEL_ROUTING_CONFIGS)
+    def test_batch_invariant_mode_preserves_uncompiled_routing(
+        self, monkeypatch, num_experts, topk, scaling_factor
+    ):
+        router = self._router(
+            num_moe_experts=num_experts,
+            moe_router_topk=topk,
+            moe_router_topk_scaling_factor=scaling_factor,
+        )
+        hidden = torch.randn(2, 1, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+        def unexpected_routing(*args, **kwargs):
+            pytest.fail("Batch-invariant routing must keep the uncompiled reference path")
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(router_module, "sigmoid_topk_routing", unexpected_routing)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(sigmoid_topk_module, "topk_scores", unexpected_routing)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(router, "_compiled_topk_routing", unexpected_routing)
+        with set_batch_invariant_mode(True), InferenceMode.active(), torch.inference_mode():
+            logits = router.gating(hidden).squeeze(1)
+            assert not router._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(logits, None)
+            ref_probs, ref_indices = router_module.topk_routing_with_score_function(
+                logits,
+                topk,
+                scaling_factor=scaling_factor,
+                score_function="sigmoid",
+                expert_bias=router.expert_bias,
+                dense_output=True,
+            )
+            probs, indices = router(hidden)
+        assert torch.equal(indices, ref_indices)
+        assert torch.equal(probs.view(torch.int32), ref_probs.view(torch.int32))
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def test_unsupported_configurations_keep_compiled_path(self):
+        logits = torch.randn(4, 128, device="cuda")
+        # Unvalidated reduction widths and expert counts retain the compiled path.
+        assert not self._router(moe_router_topk=33)._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(logits, None)
+        assert not self._router(num_moe_experts=1024)._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(
+            torch.randn(4, 1024, device="cuda"), None
+        )
+        assert not self._router(moe_router_enable_expert_bias=False)._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(
+            logits, None
+        )
+        assert not self._router()._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(logits.double(), None)
+        assert not self._router()._uses_sigmoid_topk_kernel(
+            logits, torch.zeros(4, 6, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        )
